newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah firms in narrow-range trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah firms in narrow-range trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah firmed against the dollar in slow late Tuesday trading, dealers said.
They said volume was thin on lack of fresh factors as speculation for a band widening seemed to diminish for now.
"There is not much going on. The liquidity issue was the early focus but now it seems to have stabilised," one said.
Spot rupiah was at 2,371.00/71.75 at 00915 GMT against an opening of 2,370.0/70.5. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,369.60/70.50 and 2,369.0/69.6, respectively.
Dealers said overnight money fell to 12.0 percent in the afternoon after trading at a high of 16.0 percent earlier.
They said the market was basically not tight but concern over possible higher weekly tax payments made operators nervous.
"The market calmed down as they realised liquidity was sufficient," one Japanese bank dealer said.
He said short-term swaps were also seen declining following an easing in the money market. Overnight swap was at 0.5/0.65 and tom/next swap was last given 0.45 points.
Dealers said longer-term swaps were stable.
One foreign bank dealer said swap premiums were traded at their lowest points and he did not expect further declines.

A U.S. bank dealer earlier said swap premiums were likely to be trapped at their present levels on fears that the central bank fixing might soon catch up with market rates which could induce additional liquidity and increase pressure on swaps.
He said swaps were pretty cheap but worry over induced rupiah from possible central bank buying capped swap rates.
One-month swaps were at 11.5/12.5, two at 22.00/23.25, three at 33.50/34.75 and six at 71.75/72.00 points.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention band at 2,368.0/2.560 and the conversion band at 2,368/2,416 on Tuesday.
The bank depreciated the rupiah by four points last week.
